milestones.title: First reusable regulatory qualification of an MPS
milestones.summary: At least one human microphysiological system reaches formal qualification for a defined context of use through a recognized regulatory pathway, with evidence reusable by more than one sponsor or program.
milestones.rationale: A reusable qualification would demonstrate that credibility can become infrastructure rather than remain sponsor-specific evidence.
success_criteria: Formal qualification decision is publicly documented
Context of use is explicit
Evidence package can be referenced or reused beyond one sponsor-specific decision

milestones.title: Cross-site reproducibility demonstrated for priority human-based platforms
milestones.summary: Priority NAM platforms demonstrate prespecified performance across independent laboratories, operators, and sites using shared reference materials and analysis plans.
milestones.rationale: Cross-site reproducibility is a major bridge between promising laboratory performance and reusable regulatory confidence.
success_criteria: Multi-site study is prospectively specified
Independent sites meet predefined performance thresholds
Results and protocols are publicly inspectable or regulator-accessible

milestones.title: Public animal-use baselines and displacement metrics
milestones.summary: Major regulators and funders publish baseline measures that make reductions, replacements, waivers, and avoided studies attributable to human-based methods trackable over time.
milestones.rationale: Without a denominator, claims of transition cannot be distinguished from growth in NAM activity alongside unchanged animal use. EPA demonstrates that agency-level study and animal-reduction metrics are feasible.
success_criteria: Baseline methodology is public
At least annual reporting is specified
Metrics distinguish reduction, replacement, waiver, and avoided new studies
At least two major biomedical regulators or funders publish realized denominators rather than activity counts alone

milestones.title: Structured public reporting of NAM regulatory adoption
milestones.summary: At least two major medicines regulators publish a structured, searchable record linking accepted non-animal or human-relevant evidence to the regulatory context, legacy study or evidence requirement, and resulting decision.
milestones.rationale: Current named adoption can often be reconstructed only by reading individual product reviews. FDA's accepted-method inventory and EPA's displacement metrics show that more systematic public reporting is technically feasible.
success_criteria: At least two major medicines regulators maintain a public structured adoption inventory
Records identify the context of use or regulatory question
Records distinguish animal-study displacement from broader NAM reliance
Where a legacy study is avoided, the omitted or replaced study type is stated
Named product examples or reusable precedents are linked to underlying regulatory evidence

milestones.title: Routine access to human-based-method expertise in review
milestones.summary: Funding and regulatory review systems establish durable mechanisms to bring NAM, MPS, computational, and human-model expertise into decisions where those methods are relevant.
milestones.rationale: Methods cannot compete fairly if review systems lack the expertise needed to evaluate their strengths, limitations, and contexts of use.
success_criteria: Standing expertise mechanism is publicly documented
Use is routine rather than ad hoc
Relevant review panels can access human-based-method specialists

milestones.title: Species-matched benchmarking becomes a standard validation design
milestones.summary: Human-based methods are benchmarked against existing human outcomes and species-matched legacy datasets in ways that separate model performance from species differences without commissioning new animal studies.
milestones.rationale: This can test whether a NAM predicts humans better while avoiding circular validation against animal models treated as an unquestioned gold standard.
success_criteria: Benchmark design is prospectively specified
Existing animal and human datasets are linked or harmonized
No new animal studies are required solely for benchmarking

milestones.title: International convergence on reusable NAM evidence packages
milestones.summary: Multiple major regulators accept a common or mutually intelligible evidence package for at least one human-based method or method class in a defined context of use.
milestones.rationale: Convergence lowers duplicated validation costs and increases the return on qualification evidence across jurisdictions. Independent product-level convergence is already visible, but the milestone requires reusable evidence beyond isolated product decisions.
success_criteria: Common assessment or evidence package is documented
At least three major regulators act on the evidence
The approach is reusable beyond a single isolated sponsor decision

milestones.title: Documented routine displacement of specified animal studies in multiple contexts
milestones.summary: Human-based methods demonstrably replace or avoid specified animal studies across multiple regulatory or development contexts, with the displaced study types and decision boundaries made explicit.
milestones.rationale: The transition becomes materially established when adoption changes routine practice rather than producing isolated exemptions or pilots.
success_criteria: At least three distinct decision contexts document avoided or replaced animal studies
Use is repeated across more than one sponsor or organization
Displacement is attributable to named human-based methods or evidence frameworks
At least one context demonstrates routinized use rather than an isolated exception
milestones.paper_origin: new roadmap synthesis from adoption argument

milestones.title: Composable qualification of validated modules
milestones.summary: Validated human-based modules, datasets, and computational components can be combined for new contexts without rebuilding the entire credibility case from zero.
milestones.rationale: Composability is the point at which qualification begins to compound: validated components become infrastructure for subsequent methods and decisions.
success_criteria: Regulatory or standards framework explicitly permits reuse of qualified components
A new integrated application references prior component evidence rather than repeating it
Provenance and versioning requirements are defined
milestones.paper_origin: new roadmap synthesis from reusable-qualification argument
